newsitem.title: USA: Archer optimistic on broad U.S. cap gains tax cut.
newsitem.headline: Archer optimistic on broad U.S. cap gains tax cut.

text.p: House Ways and Means Committee Chairman Bill Archer said Thursday he was optimistic that a broad-based capital gains tax cut would be enacted this year.

"I am optimistic that this year we will finally get broad-based capital gains relief. I am optimistic that we will get it signed into law this year," the Texas Republican said at a construction conference.
Asked why he was optimistic on a broad capital gains tax cut, Archer told reporters: "I think we're going to get some tax relief bill ... and that's a primary item for us to have in the tax bill."

Asked about the Senate Republican proposal to cut the top capital gains tax rate to 19.8 percent from 28 percent, Archer said there was "far more" support developing in the House for a proposal to cut that capital gains tax rate to 14 percent.
The proposal is sponsored by Rep. David Dreier, a California Republican, Archer said.

"There's developing far more support on the House side now for a bill that's being sponsored by David Dreier that has a 14 percent rate in it, which cuts the 28 percent in half," Archer told reporters.
"I think that's what we're going to be going into the negotiations talking about," he added.
No formal talks have been scheduled for the working group on taxes comprised of Archer, Senate Finance Committee Chairman William Roth, a Delaware Republican, and Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin.

Archer discounted whether that type of meeting would be the way an agreement on taxes would be reached. "I don't know whether this is all going to be determined by Senator Roth and Secretary Rubin and I sitting down in a room and then delivering from Mount Olympus a tax bill, I don't think that that is necessarily going to be what's going to occur," he said.
